column1: # Step 5 (05-spark-34-jdk17): what each scored family is worth.
# Since 2026-10-13 (user decision, product scoring) the two families are
# multiplied, not added: reward = T1 x T2, where T1 is the migrated family's
# points over its total weight below and T2 is the behavior family's points
# over its total weight below (score.py, product_reward). The weights still
# sum to 1; they now set the proportions inside each factor. Where the prose
# below speaks of a family's share of the reward, read it as that family's
# share before this change.
# Two families, as rule 5 requires, and neither below ~30%:
#   behavior   0.34   the tree still does what it did      replay + the repo's own tests
#   migrated   0.66   the build resolves Spark 3.4.4 on Scala 2.13, the
#                     toolchain that produced the jar and the forked test JVM
#                     are Java 17, and every csv read that asks the engine to
#                     infer pins date inference off at the site
# The same .34/.66 balance steps 3 and 4 settled on, re-split inside itself.
# --- why three requirements here, and why they are cut where they are --------
# This step moves four things at once -- Spark 3.3.4 -> 3.4.4, Scala 2.12 ->
# 2.13, JDK 8 -> 17, and the read sites -- and item 4.2's measurements decided
# which of the four are separate claims and which are the same claim told
# twice (NOTES 6.5.2):
#   the Scala axis    `_2.12` -> `_2.13` is a suffix on every Spark coordinate
#                     and nothing else in this repository. There is no Scala
#                     source here and the only `scala.*` the tree imports is
#                     `Tuple2`/`Tuple4`, which is the same class in both binary
#                     versions (measured: 25 files, no other scala import). It
#                     is evidence about the pom, so it lives in m1 beside the
#                     version rather than in a family of its own.
#   the JDK axis      is a family, because at this rung it is three artifacts
#                     rather than one setting: what the pom asks for, what
#                     class-file version the jar actually carries, and whether
#                     the forked test JVM is opened onto `java.base/sun.nio.ch`
#                     -- without which the suite reports 256 errors before a
#                     test body runs. `F_JAXB` is not part of it: the
#                     jaxb-api/jaxb-runtime pin `sweep.py` adds at r07 was
#                     measured inert here, because Spark 3.3.4 through 3.5.7
#                     ship `jakarta.xml.bind-api-2.3.2` in `$SPARK_HOME/jars`
#                     and it still carries the 121 `javax/xml/bind/*` classes.
#                     Nothing under src/main imports `javax.xml.bind` at all
#                     (measured, 0 occurrences); the need is biojava's, and it
#                     first bites at Spark 4.0.1, which ships the renamed
#                     `jakarta.xml.bind-api-4.0.2`. So it is step 8's
#                     requirement, not this one's, and §3's rung table has been
#                     corrected from r07 to r11.
#   the reads         the step's source work, and the only one of the four a
#                     pom cannot reach.
# So: m1 is the rung fence, four rules, 0.12. m2 is the Java-17 toolchain,
# four rules, 0.18. m3 is the reads, six rules, 0.36.
# The ordering of those three numbers is the deliberate part, and it is not a
# ranking of how much typing each takes. It is R4's question answered in the
# weights: what a configuration change alone can earn. Everything in m1 and m2
# lives in pom.xml -- a version, three artifactIds, a compiler level and an
# `<argLine>` -- so a candidate who rewrites the pom correctly and touches no
# source has done real work and has not done this step, and what that is worth
# is 0.30. m3 is the half no edit to pom.xml can reach, and it carries more
# than either of them for that reason. The automated-migrator reading, which
# is the one rule 4.3 actually binds, is stricter still: an unattended tool
# bumps `<spark.version>`, and a tool that has bumped `<spark.version>` and
# nothing else resolves `spark-core_2.12:3.4.4`, fails `m1-spark-344`, and
# earns 0.000000 of this step.
# Measured rather than reasoned, and the measurements are item 4.3's, recorded
# here when they are taken rather than predicted here now. What is already in
# hand at the close of item 4.2, off the real scanners against the real trees
#   the tree the agent is handed   17 `ast read` rows, all under src/main,
#                                  7 csv / 4 parquet / 3 orc / 3 json, and
#                                  `schema=no` on every one of the seventeen.
#                                  Six of the seven csv sites pass
#                                  `inferSchema=true` and none of the
#                                  seventeen passes `preferDate`. So
#                                  `m3-csv-dates-stated` is red on 6 rows,
#                                  `m3-csv-dates-pinned` is red at 0 against a
#                                  threshold of 6, and the `-sites-kept` guard
#                                  is green at exactly its threshold.
#   its pom                        the four rows m2 is red on, measured
#                                  (/tmp/m5facts/handed8): `jdklevel source
#                                  1.8 property` and `jdklevel target 1.8
#                                  property`, `scalasuffix 2.12 33`, one
#                                  `testjvmarg -Xmx4g` and no other, and
#                                  `classversion 52 201` on the jar its own
#                                  build produces.
#   the moved pom                  the same four facts after the move
#                                  (/tmp/m5facts/moved): `jdklevel source 17`
#                                  and `target 17`, `scalasuffix 2.13 28`,
#                                  two `testjvmarg` rows -- `-Xmx4g` and
#                                  --add-opens=java.base/sun.nio.ch=ALL-UNNAMED
#                                  -- and `classversion 61 201`. Both jars
#                                  were built by the same JDK 17 image, which
#                                  is what makes the m2 pair a measurement
#                                  rather than a belief about javac: the
#                                  handed tree compiles to 52 there too.
#   the JDK axis                   the same 15014 `ast` facts from the JDK 8
#                                  image and the JDK 17 image, differing on two
#                                  `call` lines that are the pretty-printer and
#                                  not the facts (/tmp/xjdk.log). The gate does
#                                  not move when the compiler does.
#   the tree the agent is handed   0.000000, scored end to end by
#                                  gates/rehearse-step05.sh (all eight trees
#                                  in one run, /tmp/rehearse5.log):
#                                  11 of the 14 graded rules red -- m1's four
#                                  pom rules, m2's four, m3's three -- so every
#                                  family pays nothing, the milestone is shut,
#                                  and the behaviour 0.34 is gated to 0 even
#                                  though this tree replays 140 of the 141
#                                  recordings byte for byte (measured,
#                                  build/replay-p05.sh; the one it does not is
#                                  `HarnessDriver-csvdates`, which is what that
#                                  job is for). The replay only: the
#                                  0.10 family is a different question, and
#                                  this tree answers it at 0.092857, because
#                                  its forked test JVM has no --add-opens and
#                                  13 of the 140 graded tests are all that get
#                                  through without a session.
#   <spark.version> bumped, else nothing
#                                  0.000000: one character of the pom, 10 red.
#                                  `m1-spark-344-uniform` *passes* here --
#                                  every resolved Spark artifact is at 3.4.4
#                                  -- and `m1-scala-213` does not, which is
#                                  the reason the uniform rule is not m1's
#                                  only rule.
#   the whole pom moved, no source edit
#                                  0.30: m1 and m2 whole, m3 nothing, 3 red
#                                  (`m3-csv-dates-stated`,
#                                  `m3-csv-dates-pinned` and
#                                  `m3-prefer-date-jar`), milestone shut. At
#                                  the 0.30 bar and not over it.
#   the golden solution            1.000000: 182 of 182 rules green, the
#                                  milestone open, and the c09 replay off its
#                                  own jar read **141 same / 0 different
#                                  projected, of 141** -- re-measured after
#                                  `HarnessDriver-csvdates` was recorded, so
#                                  the figure now covers the one job the
#                                  candidate's edits move -- against a
#                                  corruption control
#                                  that takes the same comparison from 0 to 1.
#                                  The handed tree read 140 same / 1 different
#                                  of the same 141, differing on that job and
#                                  on nothing else, with its own control moving
#                                  1 -> 2: the two arms together are what make
#                                  this a measurement of the pin rather than of
#                                  the image (build/replay-p05.sh, 06:25:03,
#                                  REPLAY-RC=0).
# Four more trees were scored in the same run, because a calibration that only
# ever moves the number down in the direction the author expected is not a
# calibration: the two compiler properties deleted 0.48, `<release>8</release>`
# written next to `source` and `target` 17 0.48 (the same price for the same
# jar, reached two different ways), the six inferring reads turned into json
# reads 0.30, and surefire told to skip the suite 0.000000 -- the last of them
# with all fourteen graded rules green and one standing rule red, which is what
# VOID means. The full table and its per-rule verdicts are CHECKLIST-4.2.md
# section 5; the trees themselves are derived in gates/rehearse-step05.sh.
# Those four rows are the item-4.3 calibration and they were filled in from
# the runs, not from this paragraph. The shape each was expected to take is
# written in `CHECKLIST-4.2.md` section 5, before the run rather than after
# it, so that a measurement agreeing with the prediction is a confirmation and
# not a recollection (trap 6, applied to the author) -- and all eight agreed,
# to the digit, including the four below. The third row is this step's
# own addition to the two step 4 took: at a rung whose work is mostly build
# configuration, "the pom, done properly, and nothing else" is the tree the
# weights above are aimed at, and a number that came out much above 0.30 would
# mean this file is wrong rather than that the tree is good.
# Two counted thresholds above one are graded, and both are in m3:
# `m3-csv-sites-kept` (atleast:7) and `m3-csv-dates-pinned` (atleast:6). The
# other six `atleast` rules are `atleast:1`, which is presence and not a count.
# The two are not in the same position and this file used to claim they were.
# `m3-csv-sites-kept` is a count of *sites that already exist* rather than of
# work done -- the lesson step 4's item 4.3 paid for (NOTES 6.4.8): a threshold
# over work can be cleared by a class full of decoys, while an `absent` rule
# over a per-site derived fact cannot be helped by an extra row. Its guard is
# `atleast` at the handed tree's own count, so it is not clearable by adding
# rows: adding a read site does not make an unstated read site stated.
# `m3-csv-dates-pinned` is a count of work done, and adding a row does raise
# it. What it is, exactly: a floor over the number of reads under src/main that
# both ask the engine to infer and pin `preferDate=false`. What that floor
# closes is the vacancy round 2 found -- a tree that answers by hand-declaring
# a StructType leaves this count at zero and goes red. What it does not do is
# bind the identity of the six reads the tree was handed, and it cannot:
# AstScan.java records `schema=yes` for any `.schema(` call whatever the
# argument, so "is this one of the six" is not a fact this gate has. Six
# declared originals standing beside six planted reads that ask and pin would
# meet this count. That is open, it is not repaired here, and it is written
# down in NOTES 6.5.9 rather than left for the next reader to find.
# Steps 2, 3 and 4 gate the behaviour family on a milestone, because a tree
# that did not make the move preserves behaviour trivially and the marks are
# for a tree that made it. Step 5 needs it for the same reason and a sharper
# version of it: `spark-core` is `provided`, so the replay runs in the verifier
# image's Spark whatever the candidate's pom says (NOTES 6.3.11). A tree that
# edits nothing at all replays 140/141, and passes 13 of the 140 graded tests
# without ever having opened the test JVM. Every one of this rung's fourteen
# recorded behaviour changes -- the tie orderings, the JDK-17
# helpful-NPE text, ReadLocalMmtfHadoopFile's counts -- is produced by the
# image and not by the candidate, so not one of them is a must-flip a candidate
# could earn, and 0.248643 of the family's 0.34 -- 0.239357 of the 0.24 of
# replay and the 0.009286 the crippled suite leaves of the 0.10 -- would
# otherwise be free to a tree nobody touched. The replay share is no longer
# the whole 0.24 because of the one job such a tree stops matching whole,
# `HarnessDriver-csvdates`. It is not 140/141 of the 0.24 either: replay
# weights each job by the number of scored inputs it has, 249 across the
# census and two of them that job's, and credits it with the fraction of its
# recorded blocks that match, and an untouched tree still matches two of that
# job's three. What it drops is 0.000643, and the milestone is what keeps the
# rest from being free.
# `moved` in score.py is this step's milestone. It is the conjunction of two
# predicates, both read out of the same report m1, m2 and m3 are scored from:
#   rung_adopted    m1-spark-344            spark-core_2.13 resolves at 3.4.4
#                   m1-spark-344-uniform    and no org.apache.spark artifact
#                                           resolves at another version
#                   m1-scala-213            a _2.13 suffix is present
#                   m1-scala-213-only       and no other suffix is
#                   m2-classes-17           some class of this repository in
#                                           the jar is class-file major 61
#                   m2-classes-17-uniform   and none of them is anything else
#   reads_stated    m3-csv-dates-stated     no inferring csv read is left
#                                           unpinned about date handling
#                   m3-csv-dates-pinned     and at least six reads still both
#                                           ask and pin -- the positive half,
#                                           which a declared schema cannot
#                                           vacate. A count of such reads and
#                                           not a bind on which six they are;
#                                           see below
#                   m3-csv-sites-kept       the seven csv reads are still there
#                   m3-prefer-date-jar      and the statement reached the jar
# Why each half. `rung_adopted` is what the replay is a replay *of*: without
# it the 141 jobs are a reading of the image. Its pom half is the claim and
# its `bytecode class` half is the artifact-level check that the claim was
# carried out -- a pom can say 17 and produce 52 if a plugin overrides it, and
# the jar is the thing the replay runs. `reads_stated` is the source half, and
# it is a conjunction rather than its first rule alone because
# `m3-csv-dates-stated` is an `absent` rule and an `absent` rule is green over
# zero rows: a tree that deletes the six inferring reads passes it and loses
# the replay, which is the failure this task exists to catch.
# `m3-csv-dates-pinned` is the rule that closes that vacancy, and it closes it
# as a floor over reads that both ask and pin -- six of them -- rather than as
# a bind on which reads those are. A tree that declares its way out and plants
# nothing goes red here; a tree that declares its way out and plants six reads
# that ask and pin does not, because the scanner cannot tell a planted read
# from a handed one. The identity half is open (NOTES 6.5.9); what still
# answers it is the replay, which runs the handed paths. `m3-csv-sites-kept`
# is what stops "no unstated read" from meaning "no read", and
# `m3-prefer-date-jar` is what stops a source edit that never compiled -- or
# that was made in a file the build does not reach -- from counting as one. The
# replay's 141 jobs run the jar.
# `m2-test-jvm-opens` is deliberately *not* in the milestone. It is the rule
# the `tests` half of the behaviour family already prices directly: without the
# open the suite reports 256 errors, only 13 of the 140 graded tests get
# through, the family scores 0.092857 and nearly all of that 0.10 is gone on
# its own. Gating the other 0.24 on it as well would charge twice for one
# omission.
# What the milestone costs, stated rather than hidden. A candidate who moves
# the rung completely and states five of the six inferring reads scores 0.30:
# they lose m3 to the all-or-nothing rule below, and they lose the behaviour
# family to this one. That is a cliff, it is the same cliff step 4 disclosed,
# and the handoff puts it in those words -- WORKSPACE_HANDOFF.md section 3,
# "the step is the rung *and* the reads". instruction.md states the same cliff
# in its own words rather than in these. A step is made or it is not. The
# item-6 floor -- step 4's finished solution scored by this verifier -- pays 0
# for behaviour rather than the .34 an ungated family would pay it, and its
# migrated share is 0 as well (m1 red at 3.3.4/2.12, m2 red at class-file 52,
# m3 red on six sites), so the floor is 0.000000. That satisfies item 6's "<=
# 0.5" with room and it is right for the reason it was right at steps 2, 3 and
# 4: step 5 is not paid for step 4's work, which is what `hold m04.tsv` means.
# The rule ids in both conjunctions are parsed out of `m05.tsv` by pattern
# rather than kept as a second copy here, and each one's selector is
# shape-checked before it is believed -- `read_rule_ids` in score.py refuses a
# `-csv-dates-stated` rule that is not `absent` over `ast.read` scoped to
# `src/main`, a `-sites-kept` rule that is not `atleast` at or above the handed
# tree's own count, a `-classes-17` pair that is not `atleast`/`absent` over
# `bytecode.class` naming major 61, and a `-prefer-date-jar` rule that is not
# `atleast` over `bytecode.strconst`. Each refusal is there because the rule
# text it refuses is green on the tree the candidate is handed, so weakening
# the rule file alone cannot lower the floor. score.py's selftest rehearses
# every refusal and rehearse-step05.sh rehearses them against doctored copies
# of the real file.
# Within `migrated`, a requirement scores all or nothing: every rule carrying
# its prefix must be PASS. For m1 that is trivially right -- "mostly at 3.4.4"
# is not a state a build can be in, and a pom that resolves two Scala binary
# versions is not 80% migrated but broken. The same holds for m2: a jar whose
# classes are half at 61 and half at 52 is a build that compiled part of the
# tree with something else, which is a worse answer than not having moved. For
# m3 it is the substantive choice and it is the same one step 4 made: five of
# the six inferring reads pinned is not 5/6 of the move, because the sixth
# still asks the engine to guess at a column whose meaning changed under it,
# and the claim -- "every read in this tree that infers comes back with the
# type it came back with before the move" -- is false for that program.
# migration_prompt.md's rule 8 asks for proportional credit, and what this file
# pays proportionally is the behaviour family -- the replay per block over 141
# jobs, the suite per test over 140 tests -- and the three requirements against
# each other. Inside a requirement the credit is all-or-nothing; across them it
# is not; and both documents the candidate reads say so in those words. Six
# sites is also a small enough denominator that "nearly all of them" is not a
# meaningfully different state from "all but one".
# Within `behavior`, credit is proportional and the unit is rule 7's scored
# input. The recordings are the c09 census: the same tree at Spark 3.4.4, Scala
# 2.13, JDK 17 -- this step's own rung, because a step that moves the runtime
# must be graded against recordings made on the runtime it runs on. 141 jobs,
# 91.7% coverage as measured over the 140 of them that were recorded before
# `HarnessDriver-csvdates` was planned, the map in §1.7.
# The suite's denominator is 140 and not 142 for the reason step 4 recorded:
# `CustomReportServiceTest`'s two tests hardcode a `StructType.toString()`
# rendering that changed at 3.3.4, and they are red at this rung for every tree
# including the golden one. test.sh replaces `/app/src/test` with the commit's
# own copy before the suite runs, so a candidate's correction is deleted before
# it can be scored; scoring the two would cap the oracle below 1.0 and pay the
# same for deleting the file as for repairing it. They are a precondition
# (NOTES 6.4.2), and they stay one here.
# MEASURED-AT-6: this step's wall clock, from its verifier container starting
# to its reward.json, taken off the oracle run rather than estimated here. The
# four steps before it read 24m24s, 25m31s, 27m45s and 31m40s on the run that
# certifies the shipped bytes (m27-s4-oracle-rebuilt, §6.4.11). Step 5 replays
# the same census, now 141 jobs, against the same 46-class suite, on a runtime
# one rung newer, so the prediction registered before the run is "step 4's
# figure, plus whatever JDK 17 costs at session start" -- and that prediction
# is recorded in CHECKLIST-4.2.md, not settled here.
# The 141-job replay is the bulk of it, and neither it nor the 46-class suite
# is reducible without asking a smaller question: rule 10's own instruction is
# not to shrink a fixture set to fit a clock.
# family

column4: the 141 recorded jobs of the c09 census answer the same way, compared after norm.py and projection.tsv
